title: Drift Wood #7 · the caricature
logline: Gully draws Mr. Hadley as a walrus. Mr. Hadley confiscates it. Then keeps it.

panels.composition: Journalism class. MR. HADLEY (mustache, sweater vest) lecturing at the front. GULLY in the back row drawing on a discarded draft sheet. WOOD beside him pretending to take notes.

balloons.text: The inverted pyramid puts the most important information first—

image.prompt: a high school journalism classroom, a mustached teacher in a sweater vest at a chalkboard, two boys in the back row, one drawing on scrap paper

panels.composition: Gully's drawing: Mr. Hadley as a walrus in a sweater vest, tusks, the chalk. It is, again, good.
props: a walrus caricature on draft paper

image.prompt: close-up of a ballpoint caricature on scrap paper of a mustached teacher drawn as a walrus in a sweater vest holding chalk, surprisingly skilled

panels.composition: Mr. Hadley's hand takes the sheet. Silence. He looks at it for a long panel.

characters.pose: holding the drawing, looking at it

image.prompt: a teacher standing over a desk holding a confiscated drawing and looking at it with an unreadable expression, a boy in a backwards cap braced

panels.composition: Mr. Hadley folds it, puts it in his sweater-vest pocket, returns to the board. Wood, to Gully, whispering.

characters.pose: back at the board, drawing in his pocket

image.prompt: a teacher back at the chalkboard with a folded paper in his sweater-vest pocket, two boys in the back row whispering
